root_cause: Two transformers 4.57.1 issues, neither in torch.compile. (1) generate() calls OLMoE's legacy _prepare_4d_causal_attention_mask_with_cache_position without `device`, which OLMoE still requires, so a static cache raises TypeError (worked around by torchcompile_baseline.py:legacy_mask_device). (2) The real cause of the slowness: OLMoE is not on the experts interface in 4.57.1. Its MoE block loops over all 64 experts with a data-dependent torch.where, so fullgraph fails on aten.nonzero, each expert iteration graph-breaks (about 1024 segments per forward), the resume frame guards on the expert index and module and recompiles per expert until dynamo's recompile_limit (8), and from then on runs eagerly: 92-143 ms TPOT, host-CPU bound (it moved 46% with host load). Qwen3-30B-A3B's R16 torch.compile row was measured with transformers 5.20.1, where Qwen3-MoE and OLMoE both use @use_experts_implementation (grouped_mm, _can_compile_fullgraph). OLMoE now runs that same setup: fullgraph holds, no graph break or recompile-limit warning, TPOT 3.04-12.36 ms.
evidence: verified: log_r1.txt of the 4.57.1 run shows torch._dynamo hit config.recompile_limit (8) on frames [2/8] and [6/8] and fullgraph_failure.json reports Unsupported aten.nonzero.default; the 5.20.1 run reports fullgraph=true in all 15 processes with experts prefill grouped_mm / decode batched_mm; 3 fresh processes per batch, ranges 0.63-3.44%. SM90R5_olmoe_torchcompile.csv; runs/sm90r5/olmoe_tc_grouped/.

root_cause: Two wrapper-level over-allocations, neither in MPK. (1) The wrapper copied MPK's demo CLI defaults (--page-size 4096 --max-num-pages 16 = 65536 KV token slots) while the R16 protocol needs 64+1024=1088 per request; persistent_kernel.cuh draws ceil((step+new)/page_size) pages per request from one queue of MPK_MAX_NUM_PAGES, so B1 needs 1 page, not 16 (8.00 -> 0.50 GiB of KV). (2) The binding cause: the wrapper ran --batch all, rebuilding a PersistentKernel for each of 10 (batch, output length) cells in one process, and finalize_persistent_kernel() frees the runtime's task/event/queue state but not the fused weight buffers the generated launcher cudaMallocs (per layer q/k/v into one qkv and gate/up into one gatedup, originals kept). Those are outside the torch caching allocator and never returned.
evidence: verified: mem_get_info around each build measures 9.53 GiB retained per kernel build for this model (static sum of the launcher's cudaMalloc sizes in test_rank0.cu: 8.50 GiB over 78 sites, 224 MiB per layer gatedup + 40 MiB per layer qkv). R4 log0.txt OOMs at B8 round 0 with '78.74 GiB in use, 26.95 GiB allocated by PyTorch' = 51.8 GiB non-PyTorch against 6 prior builds x 8.50 GiB = 51.0 GiB predicted (1.6% apart). Fix: one process per (batch, output length) cell plus a derived page budget; the wrapper now refuses a build whose retained-byte requirement exceeds free memory instead of OOMing inside MPK. Control separating the two causes: at B16 the derived budget is 16 pages x 4096, byte-for-byte the KV pool R4 used, and the cell passes (8.3251 ms, 3 processes) with only the build count changed from 10 to 2 -- so the KV over-allocation was real (3.8x per page, 4-6 GiB at low batch) but never the blocking fault at any cell; the retained per-build allocation was. All 5 cells now collected.

root_cause: Same two causes, reached earlier because the 61 GB expert weights leave only ~12 GiB of headroom: R4 died in the second build of the first cell (B1 kernel_N1024) at 'CUDA error at test.cu:1060: out of memory', the per-layer fused qkv cudaMalloc of layer 33 of 48. A third contributor is specific to this model: MPK allocates with cudaMalloc, which cannot draw on the torch caching allocator's freed blocks, and the wrapper's expert stacking (torch.stack of 128 experts per layer, then del layer.mlp.experts) churns ~57 GiB through that cache, so the driver saw almost nothing free when MPK's launcher started. B16 is a separate MPK defect, not memory: with 16 batched-token slots multitoken_paged_attention_hopper_impl computes wrong attention whenever MAX_TOKENS x q-heads-per-KV exceeds 64 (MMA_ITERS_M = 2; 16 x 8 = 128 for this model), which reaches the argmax as NaN, whose -1 equals the eos_token_id=-1 sentinel, so every request stops at step 64. B16 is therefore collected at the demo default max_num_batched_tokens=8, MPK's largest correct configuration for this model; a 16-request decode step takes two kernel iterations there (25.59 ms vs 13.16 ms at B8).
evidence: verified: launcher retains 0.94 GiB per build (static sum over 69 cudaMalloc sites in test_rank0.cu, 20 MiB fused qkv x 48 layers dominant); KV pool 6.00 -> 0.38 GiB at B1 with the derived budget. Fix adds torch.cuda.empty_cache() after the expert stacking and after each finalize so the freed blocks return to the driver. MPK itself is unmodified. B16 localization (two-layer random models, real head/expert geometry, teacher-forced against HF eager): (requests, slots) 16:8 and 8:8 match HF argmax at 124/128 and 61/64 tokens (max gap 0.047, bf16 ties); 16:16 NaN; 8:16 and 16:16 with a per-request cap of 8 run but match only 1/64 and 5/128 (max gap 2.81); a dense Qwen3 with the same 32 q / 4 kv heads fails at 16 slots and passes at 8, so the MoE kernels are not involved; Llama-3.1-8B (4 q per kv) is equally correct at 8 and 16 slots, so its B16 row stands. runs/sm90r5/mpk/tiny/.

root_cause: MPK 63af900 reaches a model by one of two independent paths and neither covers this architecture. (a) The demos, which this wrapper replicates, exist only for Qwen3ForCausalLM (demo/qwen3/demo_hopper.py), Qwen3MoeForCausalLM (demo/qwen3/demo_30B_A3B_hopper.py) and LlamaForCausalLM (demo/llama3/demo.py). (b) mirage.mpk.model_registry, used by MPK's own serving engine rather than the demos, registers deepseek-v3, Glm4Moe, gpt_oss, Inkling and Qwen3 (dense) only. Note the registry covers none of the three demo architectures either, so the registry refusal alone is not the reason a model is out of reach -- the absence of a demo is.
evidence: verified: get_builder() raises 'Unknown builder' for OlmoeForCausalLM, MistralForCausalLM, Qwen3MoeForCausalLM and LlamaForCausalLM alike against the registered list above; the DEMOS table in mpk_baseline.py is the operative support set. Building a task graph for a new architecture means writing an MPK demo, which would be new MPK work, not a configuration change.
